sections.content: You know the present subjunctive after wishes, emotions and value judgments from A2 Unit 27. The same subjunctive follows *recomendar que*, *aconsejar que* and similar verbs of advice: it introduces the recommended action, especially when the person giving the recommendation and the person who should act are different.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que hables con tu profesor.
items.english: I recommend that you speak to your teacher.

items.spanish: El médico aconseja que evitemos el ejercicio durante unos días.
items.english: The doctor advises that we avoid exercise for a few days.

items.spanish: Te recomiendo que no tomes una decisión cuando estés enfadado.
items.english: I recommend that you do not make a decision when you are angry.

items.spanish: Les aconsejamos que comparen las alternativas antes de elegir.
items.english: We advise them to compare the alternatives before choosing.

sections.content: When the recommendation is directed at another subject, use *que* + present subjunctive. If the same person performs both actions, an infinitive is often more natural.
